title: Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4 with words spaced, and the questions
subject: Qur'an & Tajweed
unit: Spring 1: Al-Ikhlas, Al-Masad and joining letters
source: Written for quran/y1 lesson 12 (Pupil PDF worksheet: Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4 with words spaced, and the questions)
intro: Lesson 12. Read each word slowly, pointing with your finger. Only the Arabic is the Qur'an; the English is a translation of its meaning.

arabic.text: لَمْ يَلِدْ وَلَمْ يُولَدْ (٣) وَلَمْ يَكُن لَّهُۥ كُفُوًا أَحَدٌۢ (٤)

head: Ayah
Translation of the meaning (Saheeh International)
rows: He neither begets nor is born,
Nor is there to Him any equivalent."

questions.q: Chunk and link Al-Ikhlas 112:3-4 with the teacher.
Listening turns: today's group says 112:3-4 to the teacher, one by one. Everyone else: say it softly 3 times looking, 3 times without.
questions.a: Pupil recites with no help; the teacher marks hifdh and tajweed on the rubric and gives one target.

questions.q: Say the whole of Al-Ikhlas to a friend.

questions.a: A) Nothing is equal to Allah. 112:4: there is none equal to Him.

questions.q: Al-Ikhlas 112:3: «لَمْ يَلِدْ ...» Which word comes next?
Think again: Everyone you know has a mother or father. Allah is different. How?
questions.a: Allah has no child and no parent, and nothing is like Him (112:3 to 4).
